utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I call witness X. Witness X, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Do you have the oath? Would you please take the oath that is being handed to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Madam, in Court you shall be known as "witness X". Can you confirm the following details: do you live in [redacted]?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: For how long have you lived there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since I was born.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you married or single?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Married.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What is your religious and ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have given personal details here that will need to be redacted and I believe a redaction mark has been set. Your Honour, if the details concerning the place where the witness lives could be removed from the public record?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, that request will be granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: As well as the religious and ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If possible.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: When you say "public record", you mean the video?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The transcript that is to be released and the video.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That will be granted.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could we please ask the witness to speak into the microphone?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Madam, if you would come a little bit closer to the microphones, if your chair could be brought forward a little bit, because what you tell us has to be heard by the Court and translated for us. Do you know Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: For how long have you known him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Over 20 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you friendly with the Tadic family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you related to the Tadic family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We are in open session. Of course, if you truly want it redacted -- you can handle it any way you want. I do not understand why the religious and ethnic background should be redacted. For all of the other witnesses we have asked that question, even those that have been protected, even those who were anonymous. I do not understand that. Then just in terms of the redaction, well, you can handle it however you want.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It is because this witness is capable of being identified through that information.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Through the religious and ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, as a result of where she lives currently.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: If that is redacted, where she lives currently, then is the religious and ethnic background relevant? I guess my question is that in the motion that you filed at the end of the Prosecutor's case in chief, you had indicated that all of the witnesses had a bias because of their religious and ethnic background. I am wondering now whether this is something at least relevant for the Trial Chamber. That is why I asked whether you wanted it redacted just from the video or from the transcript as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It is information for the Trial Chamber. It may be important to know about the background of this witness, but experience over the last few days has taught us to be very careful about the information we leave on the record concerning witnesses. We have had great concerns which had to be acted upon last night.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: As I have indicated, in terms of the ethnic and the religious background, I do not understand the reason, but certainly as to the others, Mr. Niemann, what is your position? But I have granted it as to the religious and ethnic background.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honours. In relation to it being material available to the Chamber, then we have no objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. I am proceeding with an abundance of caution here, your Honour, because of our experience. [To the witness]: How well did you know Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Quite well enough. I knew him very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Before the conflict started in Kozarac in 1992, how regularly would you see him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very often.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Whereabouts would that be, where you live or did you visit the family home in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were two cases of deaths in our family and he came to see us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Had you visited his family home in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you know his mother, Staka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you know his wife, Mira?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you have a friendship with Mira that was separate from your friendship with Dusko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you see the children of Dusko Tadic and his wife Mira?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your husband, did he know the Tadic family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were very good friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When building works were undertaken on Dusko Tadic's family home, did your husband have anything to do with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What did he do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He joined in when work was going on there and helped.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember when that was?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In 1992 did you become aware of a conflict in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Personally not, but I heard some rumours but we did not know anything for certain, but there was talk.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you in Banja Luka at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The rumours and talk that you heard about the conflict in Kozarac, do you know if that was at the time that the conflict was happening or later?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A little before the conflict there were rumours, but we did not know exactly what was happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What were the rumours that you heard a little before the conflict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That there were disturbances. We did not know exactly what kind because we did not have any detailed information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know at the time of the conflict in Kozarac where Dusko Tadic was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was in my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell us, first of all, about the Tadic family, his wife Mira, the children? Do you know where they were at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the beginning of May they were in Banja Luka in Starcevica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Where is Starcevica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a district in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know whereabouts in Starcevica they were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not know because I did not visit them. We were in touch by telephone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you say the beginning of May, are you able to pinpoint that by a date or perhaps a week in May when that would have been?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was around 10th May.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you see the Tadic family, being Mira and the children, in those days in May before the conflict in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I will just repeat the question. Did you see the Tadic family before the conflict in Kozarac during that time in May in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. On 23rd she came to visit me and she spent the night together with her whole family.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you say she spent the night with her family, who was that? Who was there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dusko's mother, his wife, the two children and Dusko.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you know in relation to that date when the conflict in Kozarac started?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We learnt afterwards, I think it was a Sunday, a Sunday afternoon, I think that must have been the 24th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Why did Dusko and his family come to see you then on 23rd?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They came because the conditions of life in the house in which they were accommodated were very poor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Which house was that? Where were they staying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it belonged to the Alic family, but I do not know the first name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Which house is that? Where is that house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Starcevica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is in Banja Luka, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know how long the family had been living in Banja Luka for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think about one and a half to two months. I am not sure, but I think that is about right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Dusko Tadic, when you saw him on 23rd May, do you know where he been before, where he had been living?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He brought his family at the beginning of May and then I think he went back to Kozarac and came back again on 23rd May.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What was the reason for why you can remember these details about when they came to stay with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They came about 8.30. They were highly depressed. Dusko said that he did not want to put on a uniform because he did not want to participate in the attack against Kozarac, against his neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How long did they stay at your house for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Who else was in your house at this time? You have mentioned the Tadic family. You were there. Was there anyone else in the house as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My husband, my mother-in-law (but she died) and no one else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You said that the conditions were poor in the house that they were living in in Starcevica. Did they tell you anything about those conditions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They did not have the essentials in order to be able to live. They would have to purchase things and to clean it up because there was no one living there, apparently, for some time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The house where you live, is that a comfortable and modern home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you saw Dusko with his family on that occasion and you told us that they stayed for two days, when they left, do you know where they went or where they were going to after they left your home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They went to that flat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that the one at Starcevica that you told us about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How often did you see the Tadic family in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very often, very often.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know how long Dusko Tadic stayed in Banja Luka for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When they left my house on 24th they came again a week later on a Sunday for lunch.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was Dusko Tadic with his family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: For how long did Mira Tadic and the children and the mother live in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot tell you exactly, but I will try. I think at the end of June they went to Prijedor and Dusko got an apartment there. Whether it was June or July, I cannot tell you exactly. I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did Dusko Tadic remain with his family in Banja Luka, do you know, until they left and moved to Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did there come a time when Dusko Tadic left Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not believe so. I am not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did Dusko Tadic have any work in Banja Luka at this time when you saw him there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was working in Cajevac, but I think in that period that he was not working.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you aware of any job that Dusko Tadic had, for instance, later on in the year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You told us that you did not visit the house in Starcevica where they lived. Was there any reason for that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was because at that time it was very difficult to move around in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was this house in Starcevica or this place where they lived -- I think you called it an apartment -- in a different part of the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you saw Dusko Tadic in Banja Luka, was that when he was on his own or in the company of his family or with anyone else when you saw him, during this time around the conflict in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He came twice with his whole family and a couple of times he came by with his brothers, Ljubo Tadic -- with Ljubo Tadic who also lives in Starcevica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were the brothers and Dusko friendly with your husband?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you saw Dusko Tadic at this time in May 1992, could you tell at all whether he was involved in politics?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How was his behaviour? How did he present himself to you when you spoke to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely normal, quite normal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was he dressed in military uniform in any way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Or was he carrying a weapon, any form of gun?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. That is all I ask, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Cross-examination, Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Madam, when Mr. Tadic and his family came to see you on 23rd May, how did they get to your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They came around 9 o'clock in the evening, quite late. They came on foot and were very tired.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: So that was the night-time of 23rd?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: They then left on 24th, the next day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Had you seen the Tadic family prior to that date, actually met them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We only talked on the phone.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you talk to his wife, Mira?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know whether Mira was working at the time in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You say that they stayed there until the end of June. Is that the end of June/early July, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think so, yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: During all of that time, so far as you know, Dule Tadic was not in any form of employment or working?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: At no stage during that time did you ever see him in a military uniform or any other form of uniform, military or police uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: At no stage during June did you see him carrying weapons of any form?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When your husband assisted in the building work that was carried on at Tadic's house, that was the restaurant they were building, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Or perhaps I should have called it a cafe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: A lot of people from the town participated in that, did they not? The town of Kozarac assisted with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That included Muslim people as well as Croats, possibly, and Serbian people as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Madam, I am wondering if you would look at the piece of paper I am now going to show you -- if it could be shown to the Defence first -- and also would you confirm whether or not that is your name? (Handed). Show it to the Defence first.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Madam, I am wondering if you could write down the name of your husband on that piece of paper for me, please? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann, may the Judges see that?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. (Handed). Madam, does your husband have a christening certificate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I am not sure that this may perhaps need to be written down, but I would like you to tell us the religion of your husband. If it is easier for it to be written down, then I will hand you a piece of paper and you might do that for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Could I just see that other piece of paper? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: With a pen could you write down your husband's religion? Perhaps show that to the Defence and then perhaps bring it to me. Madam, do you recall an occasion when Dule Tadic requested a copy of your husband's christening certificate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you recall on any occasion when details of your husband's religion were requested by Dule Tadic or a member of his family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Madam, have you ever given an interview to the media about the circumstances of what happened in Banja Luka and the area in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I think you said that the Tadic family came to Banja Luka on 10th May, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What day of the week was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How do you remember the day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When the 10th was?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How do you remember it was that date, the 10th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mira told me when she came that it was around the 10th.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When did she tell you that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When she came to me on 23rd.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: She has not discussed that with you since that time, has she, the particular date, when she first arrived in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Have you seen Mira Tadic at all since 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Have you ever spoken to her on the telephone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know where she is now? Do not tell me where it is, just answer if you know where she is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: But you have not seen her since 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: At no stage did you speak to Dule Tadic himself on the telephone during 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No further questions, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Witness X, in answer to my questions you said it was about 10th May when the Tadic family arrived in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you have any way of connecting that date with other events at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All I know is that I felt that something ugly was going to happen in Kozarac and they had to leave because they had received threats. They had been threatened that they had to leave Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. I ask no further questions. Do your Honours have any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection to the witness being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, your Honour, except that I think I would like to tender that sheet of paper with the name and details on it, if that could be a Prosecution Exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It should be in a sealed envelope, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: It is 350 under seal, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection, Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There is no objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 350 will be admitted under seal. Is there any objection to the witness being permanently excused, Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Fine. You are permanently excused. That means you are free to leave. Thank you for coming.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Before the witness leaves, the screens have to be placed down. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, would you call your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next is Dragolje Balta.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: This will be in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is open session.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We have to raise the blinds again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And remove the protected screen, your Honour. Dragolje Balta, please, your Honour. MR. DRAGOLJE BALTA, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sir, would you please take the oath that is being given to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is your name Dragolje Balta?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you live in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What is your occupation? What is your job?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My job, I am a locksmith. I look after locks and things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What is your ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Have you always lived in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Have you ever been mobilized in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well -- no, to a certain extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Have you ever done service in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What year was that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Have you ever done any service in the JNA since that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What other years were your service in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I was in '77, in '80, '85. Those were the military drills.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. In 1992 were you serving in any military unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Or army force?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went for a drill only, only for a military drill.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When was that in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was sometime between mid April and mid May '92.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How old are you today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I was born on 8th October 1945.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 50. Did other males of your age also have to undertake drill at that time as a result of some sort of command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I guess so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Which part of Banja Luka do you live in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That part is Starcevica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know other members of Dusko Tadic's family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do know only his relatives. I mean, mother (sic) and children and mother, and Ljubo, with him I had some contacts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When did you first meet Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the first half of May '92.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: If you look at the second last answer, that cannot be right? There is some mistranslation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps I will explore that, your Honour. [To the witness]: Which members of Dusko Tadic's family do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know his wife, his mother and two children.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I think you also mentioned Ljubo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Ljubo too, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is Ljubo his brother?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You told us that you first met Dusko Tadic in May 1992. How did you come to meet him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How was it that you met him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, because I saw him because he was in my neighbour's house and I wondered what he was doing there and that is how we met, where he was staying.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How long did he stay in that house for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, until about the end of the seventh month -- what do you call it -- July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know how it was that he came to be in that house, your neighbour's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, well, that is I wondered and I asked them and they told me that there were some troubles in Kozarac and that they had to leave it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your neighbour, was he living in that house at the same time as the Tadic family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Where was your neighbour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Where was your neighbour at the time the Tadic family were living in that house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was in Germany then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What was his name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me see, the husband, he was killed before the war, and the wife was called Ljubica, Ljubica Gorgi.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Where was she at that time in May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Germany.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember whether they came back to that house ever? Have they ever returned to that house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How did the Tadic family get into the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they had a friend, Nedim, and I guess he gave them keys because that woman left her keys with Nedim when she went to Germany, and as the house was empty they simply did him a service, that is, gave him the keys so that he could move in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Before this meeting in May 1992, had you ever seen Dusko Tadic before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: After you met him for the first time, how often did you see him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, how shall I put it? I cannot really count all the times, but we met often because we were next door neighbours. How shall I put it? Four or five times during that time, I mean, during his stay there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you in your work as a locksmith at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you out at work during the day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: About what time did you return from work usually?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, around 3 o'clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On those occasions you have described seeing Dusko Tadic, did you spend long in his company?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What were you and he doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, from time to time, a little, for half an hour, an hour, that would be meetings, have a cup of coffee or a drink, something like that, nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you get to know his wife?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you see her on occasions when you saw Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you see her on other occasions on her own without Dusko Tadic being there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you ever go and see how they were in this house next to yours that belonged to your neighbour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did. I did visit them in the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Which part of the house were they staying in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were staying in the lower part, in what we call "cellar". I do not know how to explain it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What were the conditions like of this house? How good was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: None at all. I mean, that was a house unfurnished, unequipped.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was it a house that had been completely built at this time? Was it a finished house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I do not know in what sense. It had a roof on it but nothing else, the facade had not been done, nor had it anything in it, not windows, not anything -- just a building, just a skeleton.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I would like you to look at this photograph and tell me if you recognise it which I tender to the Court now as Exhibit D62.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is Dusko.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you recognise that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do, I do. This is the upper part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps if this can be put on the overhead projector, your Honour? A copy has been served on the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Has it been offered and marked?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I do not think it has been marked yet, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Would you mark it D62?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. 62A would be appropriate.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 62A. Is there any objection to 62A?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am not sure what it is yet.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I am sorry. The Defence, though, said they tendered it to you, I thought.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: But I mean the witness has not -- I do not know what it is a picture of.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Show it to the Prosecutor first.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I still do not know what it is a picture of.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: He has told a moment ago that it was the photograph of his neighbour's house.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I am sorry, your Honour. We have no objection if it is a photograph of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: D62A will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is the building, my neighbour's house, where Dusko lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You described that as being the upper part of the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, right up to the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We can see there that there are three floors, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were the Tadic family living in any part of that house that is in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You said earlier that they were living in the basement of the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: To get to the basement of the house do you go around to the back of the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: May I show it? May I show it? Here -- is there something that I can show it with?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you just point to something, on the right, there is a photograph on the right on the projector and if you just ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- point to what you wanted to point to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is down, you have to descend there. Did you get me? Did you understand that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That you have to go down?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is right. Do you go through the front gate and turn right and go down to the back of the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Quite, yes, down there behind the house. It is the bank there, if you understood my meaning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps if would you like to look at this photograph which I tender as 60B, your Honour, D60B?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 62B. It is marked on the back as photograph 17 for the Prosecution. [To the witness]: Could you just look at this photograph, please, Mr. Balta, and tell me if you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What is it a photograph of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the photograph of that part of the house, its lower part, the basement. This is the entrance and here was the kitchen and then next to it was the bedroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps if you could put that on the overhead projector as well? Is that the back of the house where the basement is that you told us about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is an appropriate time and at this stage, perhaps, if we take our break?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to 62B? Do you wish to offer it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I was going to, yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 62B will be admitted. We will stand in recess for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: We apologise, your Honour. There was an urgent matter we had to take care of.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. I would like you now to look at another photograph, please, Mr. Balta. This is marked No. 15 for the Prosecution. If I tender it as D62C. (Handed). Mr. Balta, if you could tell me if you recognise the view in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What is it a picture of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand the question. Could you repeat it, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Could you tell me what it is a picture of? What do we see in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I see here my house and my balcony. I could point at it, but how do I do it? With a finger or?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do not worry. If you answer a few questions from me, I will be able to get you to point things out. Are there any other houses in that photograph as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What are the other houses in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you point them with a finger?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you can just tell me and then I will get you to point to it so we can see it on our video screens?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Behind my balcony, this is my house and then this is the neighbour's house where Tadic lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. If that could now be put on the overhead projector? Thank you. Is that there a photograph of the back of your house with the balcony you told us about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry, I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that a photograph of your balcony at the back of your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The house that you said the Tadic family stayed in, could you indicate that then, which house that is, on the photograph by using that pointer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can. It is ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps if you could indicate it ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here, this is it. This is the house where Mr. Tadic stayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that the front or the back of the house that you indicated there with the pointer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the back of the house. The basement is down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, I offer that now to the Court as Exhibit 62C.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to 62C?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 62C will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. [To the witness]: Were you aware of the conflict that occurred in Kozarac in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, yes, up to a certain point, yes, I heard about it. There was news and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you say you heard about it, there was the news, was that through the media, through television or radio or newspapers or from what people told you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the radio, mostly radio and television, not through people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know if you saw Dusko Tadic at that time in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean when the attack on that Kozarac occurred?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time he was in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know if he ever left Banja Luka for any substantial period of time, as far as you knew?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think -- I could not really say whether he was there for some substantial time. I did see him quite often, but .....

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you aware of the Tadic family moving out of that house in Starcevica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know or did they tell you where they were going to and where they were moving to from that house in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, as a matter of fact, I happened to be at home when we met so that we said, "Hello".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What did you become aware of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: How do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, when you were at home and you were there at that time, do you know if they were moving from the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me see. They came by car, and I saw how children and wife and mother were going and he came to say "goodbye". He said, "We are going to Prijedor, we are being given a flat there" and so we said "goodbye".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember when that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it was some time in the latter half of July. I could not be more precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you ever see Dusko Tadic in military uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Me, no, I mean, I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. That is all I ask. Wait there, please.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Cross-examination, Miss Hollis?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, you had indicated you had lived in Banja Luka all of your life. Could you tell us what was your place of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was born in the village Balta which is near Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long did you live in Balta before you moved to Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 15 years or so until I went to school.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In what opstina is Balta?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is in the municipality of Celinac, but it is very near Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In what opstina is that Celinac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Opstina? Is it in the Banja Luka opstina or is it in a different opstina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I mean Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You indicated that in, perhaps, mid April or mid May 1992 you performed military drill. Where did you perform that military drill?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: How shall I put it? We were -- I was in this Starcevica where I was born and that is where the drill was, I mean, where I lived.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What were your duties during this military drill?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we were to guard our Local Commune, I mean where I live.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You were provided weapons to do this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What type of weapons were you provided?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What type would those be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is PAP rifle, semi-automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long did you perform that military drill?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, until about the first half of May.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After the first half of May did you perform any additional military duties during 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you perform any police duties during 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you a member of any paramilitary organisation during 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was your father's name, first name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Savo.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you have sons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you tell us his name and his date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 5th May '76, and his name is Sinisa.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, during 1992 did your son perform any military duties?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did your son perform any police duties during 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was your son a member of any paramilitary organisation during 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, during 1992 did you perform any duties at any of the camps in opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You talked on direct examination about a house next to yours where Dule Tadic and his family stayed for a time. What was the last name of your neighbour whose house Dule Tadic's family stayed in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Gorgi, late Stefan Gorgi, and his wife, Ljubica.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You indicated that you believed that they had obtained keys to that house. You guessed that Nedim had given them the keys. Were you present when Nedim gave them the keys to this house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, what is the ethnic group of that family that owned that home in which Dule Tadic's family stayed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me see. Late Stefan was Ukrainian and his wife is a Croat or a Catholic, whichever way you like.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, were you a member of the SDS Party during 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You were shown three photographs during your direct examination. Can you tell us what month and year those photographs were taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Where are they, the photographs? Where are the photographs? I cannot see them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: We will retrieve those for you to look at, sir. That will be 62A, B and C.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was taken now in August, '96.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, the other two photographs, when were they taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All three of them -- no, this one was taken in '95, and this was in '95 and I think it was August again, and these, these were taken this August, '96.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, did you take the photographs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you present when they were taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You indicated that you were aware of a conflict in Kozarac because you heard about it on radio and television. What radio stations did you hear about the conflict on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, radio, Radio Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, what television station did you hear about the conflict on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Likewise, I mean Banja Luka has its television station, so we had it on Banja Luka television.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What were the dates that you heard those broadcasts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot say that. I do not remember it. I cannot remember everything.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just a few matters in re-examination:

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Nedim whom you were told gave the Tadic family the keys to the basement of the house we have seen in the photographs, did you ever talk to Nedim about this matter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you see Nedim at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Either then or after this date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Nedim was with the army then or was absent.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you were in Banja Luka in 1992 you told us about the military drill. What was your job at the time? Were you doing your ordinary job?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You told us you were a locksmith?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you working as a locksmith in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you were doing your military drill, at the time of doing the drill, were you still working as a locksmith?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: For how long did the military drill take?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sometime in the former half of May we were simply guarding that Local Commune. It was no drill.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What was the purpose for guarding the Local Commune?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know why people told you to perform this function, what the reason was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, people were to be there on duty and stand sentry there and so we did. We executed orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any recross?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If we could clarify again what commune was it that you were guarding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Local Commune of Starcevica.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The other people there with you who were guarding this commune, were they also armed as you were armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This commune that you were guarding, that was where your home is located, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is your exact address in [redacted]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if that could be redacted from the material?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, there is no objection or is there?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do not know that this was asked for before, but we certainly have no objection to anything to protect a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am grateful to Miss Hollis.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. Thank you. It will be redacted. Do you have any additional questions, Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I have no additional questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to the witness being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I am sorry, your Honour, may I confer?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would ask that he be subject to recall.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: There is no objection, I gather, to the witness returning home, but just subject to recall.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No objection to his returning home.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No difficulty with that, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Balta, you are free to return home. However, you are subject to recall which means that you should make yourself available because you may be asked to return to the Tribunal for testimony. If you are asked, then you are to return. You are now excused. Excuse me, I forgot, I am sorry, Judge Stephen. But make yourself available because you may be recalled. Excuse me, Judge Stephen has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Mr. Balta, I wanted to ask you about the drill that you undertook guarding your Local Commune in mid April or May. Did that mean that you slept away from home or were you still living in your house during that period of guarding your Local Commune?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We simply went on duty. I mean, we were -- we stood sentry so there would be -- sometimes, for instance, you would be on night duty and then, of course, we would be away from home and then the next night you would sleep at home.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: But apart from night duty or day duty for that matter, the rest of the time you would be living in your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Nothing arises, thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Balta, once again you are excused, but make yourself available because you may be recalled to testify. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Much obliged.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for coming. Mr. Kay, you will keep in touch, I suppose, so if necessary he can be recalled.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Wladimiroff will explain precisely what it means.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, would you call your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is the only Defence witness we have available at this stage in the proceedings. Due to developments last week, we could not bring over the next batch of witnesses who are now ready to come next Wednesday when the Court resumes the hearing.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I suppose I should tell you as I told the Prosecutor -- I did not tell them, I think I probably, well, I did not yell at them because I never raise my voice -- the trial has been long and I ask counsel to please not hold up the proceedings. If you are having problems about bringing witnesses, just tell the Trial Chamber and we will help you, because we did schedule Tuesday for arguments and we went all day, we went even longer than what we thought. Mr. Wladimiroff, do you want to explain more?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes, I would. As a matter of fact we had three witnesses left of last week and we anticipated to continue on L. We told you we would inform you last Monday if we were able to discuss the matter on Tuesday, but that it might also be Wednesday. You indicated that that in that case Wednesday would be available for argument. We were not able to deal with the matter, so we argued the matter last Tuesday. We learned also late that there was a postponement with L, so we were not able to bring our witnesses that quick to The Hague. We conferred with the Witness Unit and, therefore, we settled to what was available, three witnesses and L, and now we found no L and three witnesses we have dealt with. Besides that, let me read what is in the transcript, I informed you last Friday that we only had three witnesses available for next week and that we could continue on L. So you said that we will start on Tuesday and finish as soon as we have dealt with those witnesses. So we were under the impression that you were aware of what was going on.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I was very much. On your list of witnesses you had estimated two hours for one and two hours for another and two and a half for the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So we should still be sitting here listening to testimony. Once again, please have your witnesses available so we will not have any delays. We will adjourn until, next Wednesday, at 10 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Before we do adjourn there was one outstanding matter that the Court was aware of, a motion filed on behalf of the Prosecution which we have since been able to discuss. Your Honour may remember shelving for last Friday.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I do understand. I spoke with Miss Featherstone and asked her to ask counsel if they had reached an agreement on the redaction of the material. She told me at one of our breaks today that you were still working on it and I told her, thank you. Now, are you going to tell me that you have finished, I hope?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Indeed I do remember the conversation with Miss Featherstone, but since then I have been able to deal with it with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. When you reach agreement advise us and then a decision will be entered, I suppose, if agreement has been reached.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: It has, your Honour, and we do have copies of the redacted version of the purported interview. It depends upon how the Court wishes to deal with that. We can withdraw the entire package and resubmit a new package with the last attachment being redacted or we can simply provide the redacted copies of the interview and have those traded out. Perhaps it might be cleaner to withdraw the entire thing and resubmit the entire thing.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You filed the motion?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It is up to you. How do you want to handle it? What would the Registrar say if you wanted to withdraw it? I guess they would say that is OK, would they, Mr. Bos? Fine. Then you will withdraw it, submit a new motion.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: With the redaction.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Indicating that it is unopposed and then a decision or order will be entered accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is a confidential motion.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. After discussions with Defence counsel, Defence counsel has asked that again I clarify that the document which has been redacted is, in our belief, what could amount to a prior statement of the witness, portions of which would be inconsistent, portions of which would be consistent, but that is the character of what we believe that document could be considered to be. That is why we wanted to provide it to the Defence and to the Court. The affidavit from the investigator simply explained the efforts that were made after we became aware of the documents existence.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I will not even comment on that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Is that correct, Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am grateful for Miss Hollis explaining it in that way. We can accept this is a trial bench that will be able to deal with this material that concerns one of the confidential Prosecution witnesses.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: In any case, the parties have agreed as to the attachment and what will be redacted. The motion will be withdrawn and a new motion then will be filed with a redaction and we will enter an order granting it.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, since we still have some time perhaps we could also deal with the memoranda dealing with interpretation issues that arose during the trial. We had talked about that earlier.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Again, do you actually want them read into the record? Do you want them submitted as an exhibit or do you want both?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Both, if I understand what you are talking about. If either party considers that there has been an error in interpretation, then you should bring it to the attention of the Trial Chamber in open court so that it can be picked up on the transcript, and then you can file a memorandum, if you wish, but the most important thing is for it to be picked up.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: May I do that at this time, your Honour?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If I may pick through this as I go, your Honour. First of all, we are discussing a correction to the transcript that would have been taken on 18th July 1996, page 2405 line 7, page 2406 line 3, and testimony of 17th July 1996, page 2370 line 31. After a review of the audio tapes it was determined there was an error in interpretations. Both witnesses were talking about "automatic rifle" not about "submachine gun". That is one correction.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You have conferred with counsel obviously?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: We have provided Defence copies with all of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes and, we have agreed to that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour the next one would involve testimony of 1st August 1996 page 3007, line 33. Again, after a review of the audio tapes there was an error of interpretation. Line 33 should read as follows: "Dark green and coffee, light coffee. All colours were rather pale." The correction there was that originally the word "green" was interpreted as "blue". The correct interpretation is "dark green". This would refer to testimony on 9th August, page 3359 lines 32, 33. After submitting a request to the Conference and Language Services section the reply is this. As to lines 32, 33 could indeed be interpreted as follows: "It could be light but maybe it was shining in the sun, but his hair sort of went more in the direction of black." The note goes on to indicate that the content makes it possible for the sentence to be interpreted in more than one way. As to 9th August 1996 testimony, page 3294 line 19, line 19 should read as follows: "I can" c-a-n. Your Honour, there is one additional matter of a request for verification of interpretation concerning testimony that was given in closed session. Perhaps for that that could simply be submitted as part of the Exhibit which I am about to tender. I will note which part of it is and then perhaps the Registry could make appropriate corrections.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You have what, four or so or five? Do you want to admit them as separate exhibits? I suppose they should be admitted into the record, except for the last one which we will handle differently, I suppose, since that was in closed.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I was thinking I would admit them as one exhibit but A, B C, and then a portion of that could be sealed which would be the last one.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That would be the next Prosecution Exhibit in line as Prosecution Exhibit 351. That would be A was the first mention I made about automatic rifle. B was the mention about "dark green". C was the mention about the sentence being interpreted as "light but maybe it was shining in the sun". D was the correction of the line to read, "I can". E would be the correction pertaining to the testimony in closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibits 351A, B, C, D and E will be admitted. E will be handled appropriately since it was in closed session. Is there anything else?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Just for the reference, your Honour, the page of E is all I need?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it was at page 3567, line 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You should provide counsel for the Defence with a copy of those memos.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I have done that, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: We have them, but as I do not have them here I just wanted to make these notes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK, they are admitted. Is there anything else?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Anything from the Defence we can use the day for?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Sorry, no, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will adjourn until Wednesday at 10 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: (The Court adjourned for a short time)
